mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate of 0.3 percentage points or more signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where RSAFS falls > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index of 1% or more signals improving manufacturing output and economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where INDPRO rises > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) of 5% or more signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where HOUST falls > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the CPI inflation index of 0.5% or more over 3 months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance with falling inflation, which reduces discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in the unemployment rate of 0.3 percentage points or more and a decline in nonfarm payrolls of 0.5% or more over 1 month signals a sharp deterioration in labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) of 3% or more signals strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where RSAFS rises > 3% (t-test p > 0.05).
